tools.name: mcp__plugin_slack_slack__slack_read_canvas
tools.description:
Retrieves the markdown content and section ID mapping of a Slack Canvas document. Read-only.

Use slack_create_canvas to create new canvases. Use slack_search_public to find canvases by name or content.

When comment_threads is present, it lists this canvas's unresolved comment threads and the section_id each one annotates. Read a thread with slack_read_thread, passing its channel_id and thread_ts. If comment_threads_total_count is also present, the list was truncated to the most recent threads and the canvas has that many unresolved threads in total; read the comment threads' channel_id to see the rest.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_slack_slack__slack_schedule_message
tools.description:
Schedules a message for future delivery to a Slack channel. Does NOT send immediately — use slack_send_message for that.

post_at must be a Unix timestamp at least 2 minutes in the future, max 120 days out. Message is markdown formatted. Once scheduled, cannot be edited via API — user should use "Drafts and sent" in Slack UI.

Thread replies: provide thread_ts and optionally reply_broadcast=true. Cannot schedule in externally shared (Slack Connect) channels.

Use slack_search_channels to find channel IDs, slack_search_users to find user IDs (usable as channel_id for DMs).

tools.name: mcp__plugin_slack_slack__slack_send_message_draft
tools.description:
Creates a draft message in a Slack channel. The draft is saved to the user's "Drafts & Sent" in Slack without sending it.

## When to Use
- User wants to prepare a message without sending it immediately
- User needs to compose a message for later review or sending
- User wants to draft a message to a specific channel

## When NOT to Use
- User wants to send a message immediately (use `slack_send_message` instead)
- User wants to schedule a message (use `slack_send_message` with scheduling)
- User wants to create drafts in multiple channels (call this tool multiple times)

## Input Parameters:
- `channel_id`: Single channel ID where the draft should be created
- `message`: The draft message content using standard markdown. Supports **bold**, _italic_, `code`, ~strikethrough~, >blockquotes, lists, links, and code blocks.
- `thread_ts` (optional): Timestamp of the parent message to create a draft reply in a thread (e.g., "1234567890.123456")

## Output:
Returns `channel_link` - a Slack web client URL (e.g., https://app.slack.com/client/T123/C456) that opens the channel in the web app where the draft was created.

## Finding value for `channel_id` input:
- Use `slack_search_users` tool to find user ID for DMs, then use their user_id as the channel_id

## Error Codes:
- `channel_not_found`: Invalid channel ID or user does not have access to the channel
- `not_in_channel`: The user is not a member of the channel, so they could not send the draft
- `draft_already_exists`: A draft already exists for this channel (user should edit or delete the existing draft first)
- `failed_to_create_draft`: Draft creation failed for an unknown reason

## Notes:
- Drafts are created as attached drafts (linked to the specific channel)
- User must have write access to the channel and be a member of it
- Only one attached draft is allowed per channel - if a draft already exists, you'll get an error

tools.name: mcp__plugin_slack_slack__slack_update_canvas
tools.description:
Updates an existing Slack Canvas with markdown. Operations apply atomically against one document snapshot; section IDs stay stable within a batch.

Provide `canvas_id` and `sections` (≥1 entry). Each operation has an `edit_type`, a `section_id`, and `content` (see the schema and the `content` field description for canvas markdown rules).

Section IDs come from `slack_read_canvas`'s section_id_mapping and change after every update. NEVER fabricate or reuse stale section IDs — if you lack a fresh mapping from the current or immediately preceding turn, call `slack_read_canvas` first.

edit_type:
- append: add content after the section.
- prepend: add content before the section.
- replace: replace the section's content (include the heading marker when renaming a heading; a whole list/checklist is one section).
- delete: remove the section (content not needed).

Title section rules: when replacing the title section (the first section), supply ONLY a single-line title (max 255 bytes). Do NOT include body content or newlines in the title section — use a separate operation targeting a body section for additional content.

A heading and everything beneath it (paragraphs, lists, tables) is one logical unit — when moving or reordering, keep heading and body together. Replacing/deleting a heading section affects only the heading, not the content under it.

Workflow: call `slack_read_canvas` for current section IDs, pick targets from section_id_mapping, then call `slack_update_canvas`. Always share the returned canvas_url with the user.

## When to Use
- Add content to an existing canvas (append/prepend)
- Update specific sections (replace with section_id)
- Delete a section (edit_type=delete)

## When NOT to Use
- Create a new canvas (use `slack_create_canvas`)
- Read a canvas (use `slack_read_canvas`)
- Send a simple message (use `slack_send_message`)

When creating content for Canvases, adhere to the following Canvas-only rules: - The content should be formatted as standard Markdown, including headers, lists, links, checklists, tables, and other Markdown formatting. - When writing user IDs, you should format them as: `![](@U15CTCJ83)` where `U15CTCJ83` is the user\'s Slack ID. - When user references are used in their own line, they will render as larger cards, if referenced inline they will render as special text. - When writing channel IDs, you should format them as: `![](#C15CTCJ83)` where `C15CTCJ83` is the channel\'s Slack ID. can be used for multi-line content, e.g. 'line one

Use them to highlight important information, such as warnings, important prerequisites, and notices. - Do not use tables within callouts and callouts cannot be nested within other elements. ::: {.callout} This is a callout ::: - Block quotes support the following content: plain text paragraphs with inline formatting, headings, lists, and code blocks. - In block quotes, do not use any of the following: dividers, images, cards, callouts, column, tables, or blockquotes (no nested blockquotes). - In tables, block quotes are supported, but block quotes in tables ONLY support plain text paragraphs and inline formatting. The history-paging work is under way. A builder, impl-muko, has the task. It will do three things:

- **Stop the slow per-request lookup:** reads for one agent will use the agent list the serve already keeps, instead of asking hcom for it every time. That lookup alone costs about 0.22s per request.

The target is that on riko's 88 MB transcript, every request stays well under 200ms. That covers the tail read, each page back to the start of the file, and the forward catch-up. # Ask for herder web: publish which agents and files are in each space

For: the herder owner (tools/herder in ai-config). From: herder-native mission.
The change is additive and web-only. herder serve's generic `/api/state` store already does what we need.

## Problem

- Space definitions sync to the server in the `spaces` namespace. What is *in* a space (its panels) lives only in browser localStorage (`herder.web.layout.v4:<spaceId>`).
- As a result, a space opened on another device starts empty, and the native client can't tell which agents belong to which space.
- The owner uses web most of the time. Native has to show the same spaces with the same agents in them.
- Only **membership** is needed, not layout (splits, sizes, tab order).

## Ask

1. **New namespace `spaces.members`, synced like `spaces` and `notes`.** It uses the same row / last-write-wins / `state-changed` machinery, plus the same outbox and `last-good` handling.
   - Key: the space id.
   - Value: `{ members: [ {kind:'agent', name}, {kind:'file', root, path} ], updated }`.
   - Order: the order the panels appear in the dock.
   - `screen`, `folder` and `changes` panels are left out; add them later only if needed.
2. **Web → server (required).** Whenever the set of agent/file panels in a space changes (open, close, send-to-space, space close), web writes that space's member row. This includes a one-time backfill on load for every existing space, taken from its stored layout.
3. **Server → web (wanted, can follow).** When a member row arrives that lists an agent or file this browser's dock doesn't have, web opens it as a pinned tab in that space's dock, at the default placement. A member missing from the row closes its panel only if this browser last wrote it; to keep it safe, the first version never closes panels. This lets an agent added to a space in native show up in web.

## Done when

- A fresh browser, and the native client, both read `/api/state/spaces.members?since=0` and get every space's agents and files, and those match what the owner sees in web.
- Opening or closing a panel in web updates the row within a second (`state-changed` fires).
- No change to the layout storage, and no server code change.

<status>I've read the space-members ask and checked the web sync code and the server's state store; my proposal follows.</status>

This one is web-only, as the ask says. The server already accepts a `spaces.members` namespace, so no server change is needed.

**What it would do:**

1. **New synced namespace, `spaces.members`.** Each space gets one row listing its agent and file tabs in dock order. It is built on the same sync code as spaces and notes. Screen, folder and changes panels are left out, and layout stays in this browser only.
2. **Web writes the row.** Web updates the row whenever you open or close a tab, send one to a space, or close a space; the row lands within a second. On first load, web fills in every existing space from its saved layout. I'd leave preview (italic) tabs out, because the next click replaces them. Only pinned tabs count.
3. **Web reads the row.** If another device or the native client adds an agent or file to a space, this browser opens it there as a pinned tab in the usual spot. Tabs are never closed automatically in this version, so a sync can't take anything away from you.

Done means a fresh browser and the native client both read `/api/state/spaces.members?since=0` and see the same agents and files per space as your web view. A builder would do the work and a codex reviewer would check it. The sync code has edge cases, such as races between devices and missed updates, so it's worth a review.

The decision: go on this unit with part 3 included? I recommend yes. The ask marks part 3 as "can follow", but without it an agent you add to a space in native won't show up in web, which is half of what the ask is for. Because it never closes tabs, it stays safe.

content.text:
<status>space-members is merged and deployed at main 8abe94c7; seat culled, journal 282 written, missions at 2546227.</status>

Space members sync is live (main 8abe94c7). Reload the web view to pick it up.

- **What syncs:** each space's pinned agent and file tabs, which the web view saves to the server about 0.6s after you open or close one. Moving, resizing or focusing tabs doesn't count as a change. On first load every existing space is filled in, and closing a space removes its entry.
- **Reading it:** a fresh browser or the native client can read `/api/state/spaces.members?since=0` to see what's in each space.
- **Adding from elsewhere:** anything another device or the native client adds to a space opens here as a pinned tab. A sync never closes or unpins a tab.
- **Where it shows up:** in the space you're in, the tab appears right away. In another space it's there when you switch to it, as that space's selected tab.
- **Bug fixed along the way:** sending a tab to a space with only one group was being refused as "recovering". That is probably the refusal you'd seen before; tell me if it comes back.

I reviewed the code myself, as agreed, and saw no way for a sync to loop or close a tab. The builder's browser checks confirmed it. Those checks used a stand-in for the live update feed, so the live feed itself wasn't exercised; notes already sync over that same feed. All tests and checks passed, and your serve is running the new build.

One known limit: if a tab added from elsewhere can't be opened in some space, that space stops sending its own changes until the tab opens.
